problems.statement: Routing rule RR-17 sent all SlotBook tickets to an unstaffed-in-practice P4 best-effort queue (0.4 FTE, no target) and was never communicated to Arts, so SlotBook tickets wait a median 21 days, mostly idle before first action.

Communication failure: no recorded notification of RR-17 to Arts (distribution list ITS staff only, no mail trace, generic ACK-P4 with no best-effort notice); whether the verbal 2025-08-12 briefing occurred is unverifiable, so the Dean's and ITS Director's accounts cannot be adjudicated, but either way no durable notice reached Arts staff.

Lindqvist satellite campus has only 2 days per week of on-site technician cover, producing long hardware ticket waits (6.5 days vs 1.8) for Arts and Education alike, a secondary contributor to Arts' slower median.
Arts staff raise excessive trivial or duplicate tickets and so cause the slow service (ITS's framing).
Central IT is generally unresponsive to Arts across all categories (Dean's and Philosophy lecturer's framing).

The high Arts SlotBook ticket volume is driven by SlotBook being an unsupported, fragile, undocumented PHP 5.6 app with a poor ITS-Arts interface, possibly worsened by the 2025-09 SSO migration (unproven); volume spikes also reflect term start and the new category making tickets countable.

Structural misfit: SlotBook is a critical work-tool for 6 departments (about 1,900 sections per term) but sits outside any support agreement, ownership or migration plan; CampusBook cannot handle repeating multi-section patterns and no fit assessment exists, so retirement by January 2027 is unsupported.

Arts non-SlotBook, non-hardware service is comparable to the rest of the university, and Arts remote-handled categories are within 0.3 days of non-Arts; the generalised dissatisfaction is mainly explained by SlotBook, on-site delays and unexplained waiting, though the survey is low-response.
An Arts-run desk with 2 FTE transferred from central ITS would fix the problem.

causalClaims.from: RR-17 routing SlotBook tickets to P4 (0.4 FTE, no target)
causalClaims.to: SlotBook median resolution of 21 days, mostly pre-action wait
Arts gap in median resolution vs university (about 70% of the 6-day gap)

causalClaims.from: No notification of RR-17 and a generic ACK-P4 message
causalClaims.to: Arts leadership and staff perceiving ITS as unresponsive and being unaware of the best-effort status
slower on-site hardware resolution for Arts and Education

causalClaims.from: Arts raising trivial or duplicate tickets
Pre-existing SlotBook support burden and fragility
Arts staff waiting time in awaiting-requester status
causalClaims.to: long resolution for some non-SlotBook tickets (e.g. email migration)

actions.action: Send Arts a formal written notice of RR-17 and best-effort status, and revise ACK-P4 to state queue, status and expected timeframe or escalation route; add external-notification step to ITS change records
actions.rationale: Cheap, reversible, and fixes the clearest information-flow failure regardless of the disputed 2025-08-12 meeting.

actions.action: Run a joint ITS-Arts interim support arrangement for SlotBook, e.g. a defined triage target or named contact and an ownership/risk review of the unmanaged PHP 5.6 server (access, backups, logs)
actions.rationale: SlotBook drives 70% of the gap and supports 1,900 sections per term; a no-target queue on an undocumented critical system is an unmanaged operational risk.

actions.action: Commission a requirements-fit assessment of SlotBook vs CampusBook (repeating multi-section patterns) and a scoped, costed migration plan before any retirement date
actions.rationale: No fit assessment exists and the staff account says CampusBook cannot cover the patterns; the January 2027 date is unsupported.

actions.action: Review Lindqvist on-site cover (e.g. add a third day or remote-first triage) for Arts and Education
actions.rationale: On-site delay is a real, independent contributor, affecting 31% of Arts non-SlotBook tickets, but is a smaller driver than SlotBook.

actions.action: Transfer 2 FTE from the central service desk to an Arts-run desk from spring 2027
actions.rationale: Would not fix the notification failure or the unsupported-app problem, and would cut a desk at 94% utilisation that serves 8,620 other accounts and meets P2/P3 targets.

actions.action: Put all Arts tickets on the best-effort track as ITS proposes
actions.rationale: Non-SlotBook Arts tickets perform near university norms; this would worsen service for a group that is not the problem and deepen the dispute.

actions.action: Mandate retirement of SlotBook and move to CampusBook in January 2027
actions.rationale: CampusBook reportedly lacks repeating multi-section patterns and no migration is scoped, so a forced cutover risks the term timetable.

actions.action: Resolve the dispute over what was said on 2025-08-12 by assigning blame
actions.rationale: The record cannot establish it, and the fix (written notice) does not depend on it.

actions.action: Trace the SSO migration effect on SlotBook logins and ticket volume
actions.rationale: Only worth acting on if server log access shows SSO-related failures; ITS says SlotBook was not integrated.

nextEvidence: SlotBook server logs and ticket text for login or availability failures around 2025-09-08 to test the SSO link and the cause of ticket volume
Requirements-fit comparison of SlotBook vs CampusBook, including repeating multi-section patterns, plus cost of migration
Breakdown of SlotBook tickets by type (login, data fix, room clash) with time awaiting first action, plus any record of what Arts was told in August 2025
output.summary: Arts' slowness is real but narrow. SlotBook tickets (42% of Arts volume) were routed by RR-17 to a 0.4 FTE best-effort queue with no target, giving a 21-day median, mostly idle wait, and explaining 70% of the gap. Arts was never durably notified, and the generic acknowledgement hid the status. Lindqvist's two-day on-site cover is a second cause. Other Arts remote tickets match university norms, so neither 'ITS is generally unresponsive' nor 'Arts over-ticket' holds. The root issue is an unowned critical app plus poor information flow. Do not transfer 2 FTE, impose a blanket best-effort rule or force a January CampusBook cutover. Fix notice, set interim SlotBook support, assess fit, review Lindqvist cover.
